children: The seven-week slide marks the first such losing streak for the benchmark indices since the Covid-19 pandemic period

Indian equity markets recovered on 25 September, with the Nifty reclaiming the 23,100-mark and the Sensex gaining more than 300 points, but the rebound was not enough to prevent the benchmark indices from extending their losing streak to seven consecutive weeks.

The Sensex closed 315 points, or 0.43 per cent, higher at 73,896, while the Nifty gained 77 points, or 0.33 per cent, to end at 23,141. The Nifty Bank rose 142 points to 55,580, while the Nifty Midcap index declined 84 points to 60,906.

The seven-week slide marks the first such losing streak for the benchmark indices since the Covid-19 pandemic period. The Nifty fell around 1 per cent this week, taking its cumulative decline over the seven-week period to nearly 6 per cent. The Sensex fell 0.6 per cent during the week, while the Nifty Bank and Nifty Midcap indices declined around 2 per cent each.

Friday's recovery was led by select financial and automobile stocks. Axis Bank and Bajaj Finance were among the top Nifty gainers, while HDFC Bank rose 1 per cent amid expectations of an announcement on its next chief executive officer.
Most automobile stocks also recovered, with Mahindra & Mahindra rising 2 per cent to emerge as one of the day's strongest performers.

Banking stocks remained active amid developments around lenders. IDBI Bank gained 2 per cent after reports that the government was evaluating revised bids, while Jana Small Finance Bank rose amid expectations of a potential deal announcement. Federal Bank, however, declined.
The broader market failed to match the benchmark recovery. Market breadth was only mildly positive, with the advance-decline ratio at 5:4, while the Nifty Midcap index ended lower.

Hospital stocks remained under pressure, with Max Healthcare Institute and Fortis Healthcare declining 3-5 per cent. PB Fintech fell 4 per cent, extending its losses from the previous session, while TurtleMint dropped 20 per cent.

Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) declined 3 per cent as investors booked profits after the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) approved foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) for trading in non-agricultural commodity derivatives.
Among mid-cap stocks, Kaynes Technology, Supreme Industries, Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (Ireda), Blue Star and Manappuram Finance were among the notable gainers.

The weekly performance remained broadly weak across the market. Information technology (IT) stocks were the biggest sectoral laggards, with the sectoral index falling 2 per cent, while fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) was the only major sectoral pocket to post a stronger performance, gaining 1 per cent over the week.
